title: Phase / parental transmission for one case: is it available, and is there a private channel for the two loci?

latest.raw:
Hello, and thank you for running this.

Our leading recessive hypothesis for the case contains two heterozygous BUB1B variants. The supplied singleton VCF contains no read-backed phase linking the two loci, and no parental data is available to us, so we cannot establish whether the two alleles are in trans.

Could you tell us whether parental transmission or clinical phase was established for these two specific variants? Transmission or phase status alone would be enough - we are not requesting parental sequence data, raw files, or any recontact with the family.

We have deliberately not included the two variant identities in this public post. If you confirm a channel you consider appropriate, we will send the exact loci privately to you there.

Thank you,
Xavier Ramos (@xaviramram)

latest.raw:
Hi @xaviramram ,

Thank you for how carefully you framed this.
 Redacting the loci publicly and asking us to confirm an appropriate private channel first is exactly the right instinct, and we don't take that for granted.

Having thought it through, though, we're not able to confirm or deny transmission/phase status for specific candidate variants during the challenge — even privately, and even without seeing the exact loci. The reason is that for a two-variant compound-het hypothesis, confirming trans-phase is functionally equivalent to confirming your hypothesis is correct. That's precisely the determination Track 1 asks participants to make independently, so answering this for one team — even quietly — would give that team privileged access to the answer that other participants don't have, which we don't think is fair regardless of the channel it happens through.

A few things that might help without crossing that line:
- Any information already in the public domain (published literature, the family's own public communications) is fair game to build your case on — nothing about our declining this request should be read as discouraging strong literature-based or public-database research.
- We're aware this same fairness question applies more broadly (e.g., reference genome details raised elsewhere), and our approach is: if information like this gets shared, it goes out to all participants simultaneously, never to one team privately. We're not planning to disclose phase information before the challenge closes, but we'll keep this in mind for what we share once judging begins.

Really appreciate the rigor you're bringing to this — and sorry this isn't the answer you were hoping for.

Best,
Gaia
